Founder & Servant Leader

Dan Trinidad

CEO & Founder · Partners Mortgage

Dan founded Partners in 1988 with one unwavering belief: everyone matters. Customers, referral partners, the community, and above all, the people on his team. That philosophy hasn't shifted in 37 years.

He entered the industry as a loan officer, became a top producer at a Savings and Loan in Saratoga, then left to start Partners. Under his leadership the company has funded over 60,000 loans and become one of the most respected independent mortgage companies in the country.

Partners For A Cure

Motivated by the loss of his wife to cancer, Dan founded Partners For A Cure in 2011. What began as 20 teammates has grown into over $1 million raised for the Leukemia & Lymphoma Society.

The Modern Mortgage Bank, in three principles

Each one treats you as a partner.

Principle 01
Radical Transparency
"Real partners show their work." Open pricing, honest margins. You and your clients see every number, every step.
Principle 02
Client-First Flexibility
"Real partners trust you with every tool." When brokering wins for your client, we broker. When banking delivers more, we bank.
Principle 03
Lean by Principle
"When we stay lean, partners earn more." Flat structure, carefully chosen tools. Every dollar flows to your comp, your marketing, your clients.

Transition plan

Producing from day one.

Leif Potter — Transition Manager · with Tiffany
Submitting new loan applications

Any potential new applications you receive during the transition can be sent to whyleifpotter.com until your ARIVE credentials are issued. When submitting a file, email Leif any details you have on the borrower or scenario.

  • Leif runs credit once authorization is provided
  • Tiffany begins the pre-approval process
Pre-approval & file review

Once the borrower is pre-approved, Leif schedules a screen-share session with you to:

  • Review the file
  • Run pricing
  • Select the appropriate program and lender
Communication & visibility

Tiffany copies you on all borrower communications. Once your ARIVE credentials are active, you also have full visibility into file activity and communication within the platform.

Scenario support

Leif is your primary point of contact for:

  • Loan scenarios
  • Program guidance
  • Pricing
Our commitment

Leif and Tiffany treat every client as if they were their own. They are an exceptional team dedicated to providing a smooth, professional experience for both you and your borrowers — from start to finish.

How we work · Loan Officer

Loan Officer responsibilities.

Essential duties & workflow overview — you stay on relationships and strategy; your LOA and processor carry the file.

Lead engagement & intake
  • Make initial contact with lead and send the ‘Apply Now’ link
  • Follow up regularly until the application is submitted
  • Notify LOA once the application is in; provide borrower / preapproval context
Application & preapproval
  • Pull credit report (if LOA is unlicensed)
  • Once LOA confirms borrower is ready and provides base numbers: conduct a strategic consultation to explore loan options and scenarios
  • Issue the official Pre-Approval Letter once structure is decided
  • Notify LOA of final structure; update ARIVE and CRM notes
Preapproval to contract
  • Maintain borrower communication from preapproval through contract acceptance (purchase) or decision to proceed (refi / HELOC)
  • Once in contract, email LOA: final loan structure (amount, rate, investor), fully executed purchase contract (if applicable), escrow / title information
Locking & disclosures
  • Once LOA uploads to the investor portal: lock the loan (or give a licensed LOA lock guidance if floating)
  • Confirm all pricing details including discount / origination points for disclosures
Pipeline communication & problem-solving
  • Communicate status updates to borrower and agents throughout the loan
  • Notify borrower when contingencies are met
  • If a loan is suspended or has underwriting, appraisal, or condition issues: LO communicates directly with the borrower and collaborates with LOA and processor on resolution strategies
Closing coordination
  • Follow up with the processor consistently from underwriting through funding
  • Coordinate signing with borrower and escrow
  • Ensure a smooth, timely close and a positive borrower experience
How we work · Loan Officer Assistant

Loan Officer Assistant responsibilities.

Essential duties & workflow overview — the engine room behind every file.

File setup & application review
  • Review new applications; structure the ARIVE file per LO notes
  • Pull credit report (if licensed)
  • Review, approve, rename and organize all documents uploaded to ARIVE or emailed
Borrower communication & docs follow-up
  • Prepare and send the needs-list email to borrower, CC the Loan Officer
  • Follow up until all documents and information are received
Income & preapproval prep
  • Send employment verifications; accurately calculate qualifying income (income worksheet provided)
  • Once docs and income are complete, prepare the base preapproval summary and send to LO
Contract intake & escrow coordination
  • Once in contract or ready for refi / HELOC: receive the fully executed contract and escrow details
  • Send the escrow request and save documents to ARIVE
File structuring & property research
  • Comprehensively review the contract; complete ARIVE file setup
  • Pull property details and tax bill; calculate property taxes (tax worksheet provided)
  • Research HOA or solar through Zillow, Redfin, etc.
Lock preparation & investor upload
  • Prepare an updated needs list; update borrower on next steps
  • Confirm investor with LO; upload the .XML FNMA file to the investor portal
  • Confirm lock guidance and discount / origination point details
Loan submission & processing
  • Prepare the Underwriter Cover Letter summarizing the loan (template provided)
  • Complete the ‘Loan Setup’ tab in ARIVE; send the submission email to the processor
  • Attach title fee sheet, lock (if applicable) and cover letter
Disclosures & underwriting prep
  • Follow up with borrower until disclosures are signed
  • Once signed, review documentation and confirm readiness
  • Notify processor with final structure, document status, and underwriting readiness

How everyone gets paid

At Partners, we run payroll every day.

Most companies cut checks twice a month. Our 1099 loan officers are paid the moment a funded file is approved — money goes out the door every single business day.

1099 loan officers
Paid the day your file is ready.

Your commission follows the loan, not the calendar. As soon as a file funds and your breakdown is approved, payment is sent by ACH the next business day.

Partners runs payrollEvery day
Correspondent files

Typically purchased by the investor about 7–9 days after funding. Once purchased, we prepare your commission breakdown from the funding figures and purchase advice. Check purchase status in ARIVE or with your funder.

Brokered, HELOC & reverse files

Once we receive the check or wire from escrow or the lender, we prepare your commission breakdown for review.

01File funds

Loan is purchased, or the wire / check is received.

→
02Breakdown sent

You receive your breakdown, generally within 1–2 business days.

→
03You review

Respond ASAP to approve or flag any corrections.

→
04Paid via ACH

Approved commissions are sent the following business day.

A quick note on timing. Turnaround can vary slightly with volume — our target is 1–2 business days once we have what we need to process. The faster you review and approve your breakdown, the faster your commission goes out the door.
W-2 loan officer · commission earners

Paid semi-monthly — the 15th & last day of the month.

W-2 employee · salaried & hourly

Paid semi-monthly — the 15th & 30th of each month.

Fees, bonuses & what is included

What it costs — and everything you get.

One flat monthly Foundation covers your entire technology and marketing stack. Here is the full breakdown, plus how per-file processing and team bonuses work.

Your Foundation
$175/month

All technology, marketing, and support. One flat fee, no add-ons, no surprises.

Processing collection
$795required

Collected on every file. You can raise it to $1,095 to cover the bonuses.

Team bonuses
$300per file

$150 LOA bonus and $150 processor bonus, paid by the loan officer.

You choose how the bonuses are funded. Collect the standard $795 and pay the $300 in bonuses ($150 LOA plus $150 processor) from your commission — or raise the processing collection to $1,095, and the additional $300 covers both bonuses with nothing out of your comp.
Brokered files with no embedded fee. When a loan is brokered and the lender does not include an embedded processing fee, or you waive processing for the borrower, a flat $400 processing charge applies to you. Partners absorbs the rest, so we are effectively splitting the cost with you rather than passing it along in full.

Candidate Name
Dear Candidate,
W-2 Position

We’re thrilled to extend an offer for you to join Partners Mortgage as a Loan Officer! At Partners, we don’t just hire loan officers — we empower mortgage professionals to thrive, grow, and make a real impact. You’re being invited into a company with a bold vision, strong leadership, and a supportive culture where your potential is truly the limit.

Compensation

The following structures your compensation for closing loan files with Partners Mortgage:

Lead sourceCompensation
Why Partners Mortgage?

We’re more than just a mortgage company. At Partners, you’ll gain access to:

  • 200+ lenders for unmatched client solutions
  • Out-of-state referral program to expand your reach
  • Advanced tools & tech to streamline your workflow
  • Top-tier support to help you scale faster
  • Collaborative, growth-focused culture
  • A platform for long-term success
Next steps

To accept this offer, simply send a confirmation email to peter@partnersmortgage.com

This letter outlines the key terms of our offer. While we’re excited about the future, please note that employment is at-will — either you or Partners Mortgage may end the relationship at any time. This offer does not constitute a contract, and terms are subject to change.

This letter of intent is extended in good faith and remains open for acceptance through —, fourteen (14) days from the date of this letter. After that date, the terms outlined above will lapse in their entirety — though we would welcome the conversation anytime.

We’re genuinely excited about the opportunity to work together and welcome you into our growing family. Let’s do great things!

Sincerely,
